curriculum: The 2026–27 regulations specify 135 EC in the major plus 45 EC of profiling. The major includes eight 7.5 EC first-year courses, 7.5 EC of required biochemical methods and academic skills and a 15 EC chemistry thesis (82.5 EC). The selected 52.5 EC of major electives comprises 37.5 EC at level 2 and 15 EC at level 3. The example takes molecular modelling and structure determination in category 1, Biochemistry 2 in category 2, and Physical Chemistry 2 and Inorganic and Solid-State Chemistry in category 3. Solids and Surfaces and Advanced Physical Chemistry are level-3 major electives. Molecules and Materials is an illustrative direction; it is not a named requirement or distinct degree. The earlier Molecular Life Sciences track is discontinued and is not the Molecules and Life interest direction.
progression: Table 1.1 requires at least 45 EC at level 3 across the whole degree. The major contributes 30 EC at level 3 including the thesis, leaving at least 15 EC of level-3 profiling in this example. This also meets the profiling requirement of at least 15 EC at level 2 or 3. The two generic profiling slots total 45 EC and are not assigned fictitious courses. The thesis requires 120 earned EC and commonly takes place in the final period, with timing arranged with a research group. The example places foundational chemistry and mathematical and experimental methods before the advanced materials and physical chemistry courses. Physical Chemistry 2 precedes Advanced Physical Chemistry. Article 3.3 establishes Dutch as predominant at level 1, both Dutch and English at level 2, and English at level 3.
